name: manual_a31e13
claim: A bare 'cd <dir> && <command>' in this Bash tool persists the cwd change to EVERY subsequent command in the session — it does not scope to that one line the way a subshell would. When checking a worktree/branch other than your main working tree (e.g. 'cd .claude/worktrees/X && git status'), always cd back to the main repo root immediately after, or use 'git -C <dir> <cmd>' instead of a bare cd to avoid drift.

decisions.notes: Drifted into .claude/worktrees/stm-pattern-integration (branch docs/stm-pattern-integration, an old pre-PR#205 checkout) after checking that worktree's git status during a stale-claim investigation, then unknowingly ran grep/git commands against the wrong checkout for several turns. No data loss (Edit/Write tool calls used absolute paths and landed correctly; the coordination board resolves via git-common-dir regardless of cwd), but caused real confusion diagnosing a false 'my gate edits are gone' alarm.
